newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates rose in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates rose in latest week.

text.p: Interest rates on fixed-rate mortgages rose in the latest week but adjustable-rate loans edged lower, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

The average commitment rate on 30-year loans rose to 7.67 percent this week from 7.64 percent last week and 15-year loan rates inched up to 7.18 percent from 7.16 percent, the agency, known as Freddie Mac, said.
One-year adjustable-rate loans dipped to an average 5.56 percent from 5.57 percent, it said.
A year ago, 30-year loan rates averaged 7.02 percent, 15-year rates were 6.56 percent, and one-year adjustables stood at 5.46 percent.
"Rates rose a little earlier in the week and that may well be reflected in slightly higher interest rates in the coming week," Robert Van Order, Freddie Mac chief economist, said.
"Still, we expect interest rates to remain in the 7.5 percent to 8 percent range at least for the foreseeable future," he said.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30- and 15-year loans in the week, both unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on adjustable-rate loans, up from 1.3 percent the previous week.
